parts:

I thought perhaps these warnings might mean that there was something wrong with my Rcpp library, but the "hello world" test function seems to work: 

> # using library inline to compile a C++ code on the fly
> library(inline) 
> library(Rcpp)
Attaching package: ‘Rcpp’
The following object is masked from ‘package:inline’:
    registerPlugin
> src <- ' 
+   std::vector<std::string> s; 
+   s.push_back("hello");
+   s.push_back("world");
+   return Rcpp::wrap(s);
+ '
> hellofun <- cxxfunction(body = src, includes = '', plugin = 'Rcpp', verbose = FALSE)
> cat(hellofun(), '\n') 
hello world 

Can anyone illuminate my issue or suggest next steps? My hope is that eventually we can track down the source of my hanging consoles...

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: warnings when installing STAN
parts:
On Wednesday, April 16, 2014 4:50:07 PM UTC-4, Christopher Chatham wrote:
Can anyone illuminate my issue or suggest next steps? My hope is that eventually we can track down the source of my hanging consoles...

Those unsequenced warnings only pertain to the parser, probably were never harmful, and have already been fixed in the develop branch of Stan. If you are having trouble with hanging when running a model, that is almost certainly a different issue.

Ben
